why: A matrix whose rows continue one another is one sorted array laid out in rows: binary search the cell number k in [0, rows*cols) and read matrix[k // cols][k % cols].
hints: Read the matrix row by row. Is the sequence you get sorted?
Yes, so search it as a single array of rows*cols values. You only need to turn a flat index into (row, column).
lo, hi = 0, rows*cols - 1; v = matrix[mid // cols][mid % cols]; usual three-way compare. O(log(rows*cols)). (Two searches, first the row then the column, also work.)
pitfalls: Empty matrix: return false before computing cols.
Use the column count for both // and %, not the row count.
